Mean and Variance of Extreme Value Distributions

Source: R/mextreme.R
extreme-value-moments.Rd

Computes the mean and variance of common extreme value distributions given their parameters.

mgumbel(loc = 0, scale = 1)

mfrechet(loc = 0, scale = 1, shape = 1)

mrweibull(loc = 0, scale = 1, shape = 1)

mgev(loc = 0, scale = 1, shape = 0)

mgpd(loc = 0, scale = 1, shape = 0)

mgompertz(shape, rate = 1)

Arguments

loc

location parameter.

scale

scale parameter.

shape, rate

vector of shape and rate parameters.

Value

A named numeric vector with elements mean and variance. Returns NA where moments do not exist.

Details

Gumbel:
\(\mu = a + b\gamma\)
\(\mathrm{Var}(X) = \frac{\pi^2}{6} b^2\)
where \(\gamma \approx 0.5772\) is the Euler-Mascheroni constant, \(a\) = loc and \(b\) = scale.

Fréchet:
\(\mu = a + b\,\Gamma(1 - 1/s) \quad (s > 1)\)
\(\mathrm{Var}(X) = b^2\left[\Gamma(1 - 2/s) - \Gamma(1 - 1/s)^2\right] \quad (s > 2)\)
where \(a\) = loc, \(b\) = scale and \(s\) = shape.

Reverse Weibull:
\(\mu = a - b\,\Gamma(1 + 1/s)\)
\(\mathrm{Var}(X) = b^2\left[\Gamma(1 + 2/s) - \Gamma(1 + 1/s)^2\right]\)
where \(a\) = loc, \(b\) = scale and \(s\) = shape.

GEV:
For \(s = 0\) (Gumbel), \(s > 0\) (Fréchet) and \(s < 0\) (Reverse Weibull), the moments are computed accordingly. Mean exists for \(s < 1\), variance for \(s < 1/2\).

GPD:
\(\mu = a + \frac{b}{1-s} \quad (s < 1)\)
\(\mathrm{Var}(X) = \frac{b^2}{(1-s)^2(1-2s)} \quad (s < 1/2)\)
where \(a\) = loc, \(b\) = scale and \(s\) = shape.

Gompertz:
For \(a > 0\) the moments are computed numerically via integration. For \(a = 0\) the distribution reduces to the exponential with \(\mu = 1/b\) and \(\mathrm{Var}(X) = 1/b^2\). For \(a < 0\) the moments do not exist (NA).

References

Coles, S. (2001) An Introduction to Statistical Modeling of Extreme Values. Springer.

Kotz, S. and Nadarajah, S. (2000) Extreme Value Distributions. Imperial College Press.

See also

dgumbel, dfrechet, drweibull, dgev, dgpd

Examples

mgumbel(loc = 0, scale = 1)
#>      mean  variance 
#> 0.5772157 1.6449341 
mfrechet(loc = 0, scale = 1, shape = 3)
#>      mean  variance 
#> 1.3541179 0.8453031 
mrweibull(loc = 0, scale = 1, shape = 2)
#>       mean   variance 
#> -0.8862269  0.2146018 
mgev(loc = 0, scale = 1, shape = 0)
#>      mean  variance 
#> 0.5772157 1.6449341 
mgev(loc = 0, scale = 1, shape = 0.3)
#>      mean  variance 
#> 0.9935178 5.9245766 
mgev(loc = 0, scale = 1, shape = -0.3)
#>      mean  variance 
#> 0.3417643 0.9784633 
mgpd(loc = 0, scale = 1, shape = 0.3)
#>     mean variance 
#> 1.428571 5.102041
